#4351 -- is -remove-unused-globals parsed and honoured?

Produced by `python flagcheck.py`. Every case is the same dxr.exe over
the same repro.hlsl, differing only in the token occupying the
-remove-unused-globals slot. sha256 is over combined stdout+stderr.

  `struct Child` is the definition this issue says is wrongly removed.
  The `// Rewrite unchanged result:` banner is printed by
  tools/clang/tools/libclang/dxcrewriteunused.cpp:1087 only when
  NEITHER -remove-unused-globals NOR -remove-unused-functions was set,
  so it is a positive marker of which code path the run took -- which
  exit status alone cannot tell you.

           case  exit  struct Child  unchanged banner  sha256(first 16)
--------------- ----- ------------- -----------------  ----------------
      real-dash     0       REMOVED                no  f70a7e2565ffb2ee
     real-slash     0       REMOVED                no  f70a7e2565ffb2ee
         absent     0       present               yes  7b4e730f9339264a
 nonsense-slash     0       REMOVED                no  f70a7e2565ffb2ee
  nonsense-dash     1           n/a               n/a  81795e9205ea9925
     misspelled     1           n/a               n/a  d76bf27772c3fbe0

WHAT EACH CASE IS FOR

  real-dash       the reporter's spelling, exactly as filed
  real-slash      MSVC-style prefix of the same option
  absent          baseline: the option removed entirely
  nonsense-slash  SKILL.md's silent-ignore control, alongside the real option
  nonsense-dash   the same nonsense with a '-' prefix
  misspelled      the real option minus one character -- proves the exact spelling is what the parser recognises, so real-dash was not an accidental near-match

READINGS

  [PASS] real-dash differs from absent
         the option changes the output, so it is parsed and honoured -- not silently ignored
  [PASS] the difference is exactly the removal under test
         with the option, `struct Child` is gone; without it, `struct Child` is present -- so the removal is attributable to this option and to nothing else in the command line
  [PASS] real-dash and real-slash are byte-identical
         both spellings of the real option reach the same code
  [PASS] nonsense-slash is byte-identical to real-dash
         /ZZZNONSENSE exits 0 and does nothing: a clean exit proves nothing about a '/'-prefixed flag, exactly as SKILL.md warns
  [PASS] nonsense-dash is diagnosed
         the '-' prefix IS validated by dxr's own option parse, so the silent-ignore hazard is specific to '/'
  [PASS] misspelled is diagnosed
         the parser recognises the exact spelling
  [PASS] the unchanged-rewrite banner tracks the option
         confirms match.json clause 4 is a valid in-run self-test that a rewriter option was honoured


VERBATIM

=== real-dash ===
$ <repo>/build/Debug/bin/dxr.exe -E InitArgs -remove-unused-globals repro.hlsl
[exit] 0
[sha256] f70a7e2565ffb2ee5aad0f94d97a3f06766d69857ea416692ddd1b8638ce7cb2

struct Parent {
  Child MultipleChildren[2];
};
RWStructuredBuffer<Parent> ParentBuffer;
[numthreads(1, 1, 1)]
void InitArgs() {
  ParentBuffer[0] = (Parent)0;
}

  ParentBuffer[0] = (Parent)0;

=== absent ===

// Rewrite unchanged result:
struct Child {
  uint Test;
};
struct Parent {
  Child MultipleChildren[2];
};
RWStructuredBuffer<Parent> ParentBuffer;

void InitArgs() {
  ParentBuffer[0] = (Parent)0;
